narrative.northStar: The Camera Display Over a Render Loop
narrative.overview:
The overlay reads the way a technical camera display reads over a live image. Indicators hug the edges of the frame and the centre always belongs to the scene. There are no panels and no cards: values are drawn straight onto the canvas in white condensed tabular numerals, each with a 1px dark contour so it stays legible on any image. Containers exist only where a camera display would use them: small dark plates with a 1px white border for state (backend, DISP, toggles), the DISP menu, the tooltip, and the info pages.

Density is high but disciplined. Detail is set by levels (display modes cycled with DISP), never all at once. Positions are fixed per mode, so numbers never jump between frames. Colour is almost absent: the readout is ink on image. Yellow is the only voice for "look here", red means a budget badly missed, and the three series colours (red, green, blue) appear only while the graph that uses them is on screen, where they add up like light.

Motion is mechanical and edge-bound. When a mode changes, elements that move glide to their new grid cell. Elements that leave slide out past the nearest edge of the overlay and never fade in place. Under reduced motion, changes are instant.
keyCharacteristics: White condensed tabular numerals with a 1px dark contour, with no backing panel.
Values sit beside their labels. Labels are short uppercase pairs stacked to one side of the number.
Dark plates with a 1px white border are the only filled containers in the readout layer.
Square corners everywhere. Every line is 1px and lands on whole pixels.
Additive RGB graphs: channels meet in white, and one contour surrounds their union.
Yellow for alert and current choice, red for out of range, everything else ink.
A fixed corner grid with a free centre. Nothing animates except layout changes.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Look Rule
rules.body: Yellow is reserved for alerts and for the current choice. It never decorates, never labels a series, and never fills an area except the checked menu row.

rules.name: The Colour Only With Its Graph Rule
rules.body: The labels of a readout carry the CPU and GPU series colours only while the Performance graphs are on screen. In every other mode they go back to ink. Glyphs and dials always stay ink, even inside an alert or a coloured label.

rules.name: The Alerts Change Colour Only Rule
rules.body: An alert changes the colour of a value and nothing else: no weight change, no size change, no badge. The layout never moves.

rules.name: The Beside Not Above Rule
rules.body: A label sits beside its value, never above it as a heading. Numbers hug their label: a number before a unit or plate is right-aligned, and a number after a stacked label is left-aligned. The reserved width (a minimum width in `ch`) stays on the far side.

rules.name: The Contour Rule
rules.body: All text on the canvas carries a 2px stroke in contour colour painted under the fill (`paint-order: stroke fill`), so exactly 1px of contour shows outside each glyph. Text inside plates, the menu and the tooltip has no stroke, because those already sit on a dark ground.

rules.name: The Free Centre Rule
rules.body: Every element lives in an edge cell. A new component gets a grid area at an edge, takes its gaps from the spacing scale, exits past its nearest edge, and hides in Off.

rules.name: The Contour Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separation from the image is always a centred 1px dark contour: text-stroke for text, geometry 1px wider for glyphs and graphs, spread-only box-shadow for boxes. Plates never get a contour.

dos: Do draw every value straight onto the canvas in ink, with the 1px contour (2px stroke painted under the fill).
Do take every gap from the spacing scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24), and give every new element an edge grid cell.
Do put labels beside values as short uppercase stacked pairs, and keep numerals tabular with a reserved width.
Do use a plate (1px ink border, plate-grey, square) for any state code or control.
Do signal an alert by changing colour to signal yellow only, and reserve clip red for a badly missed budget.
Do show unavailable metrics as an em dash, a dashed dial, or an empty graph, never as zero.
Do composite overlapping series additively and surround their union with one contour.
Do make leaving elements exit past the nearest edge in 280ms, and respect reduced motion.
Do render glyphs at 16px or a multiple of it, with ink in currentColor and the category shown by the container.
donts: Don't put a backing panel or card behind the readouts. The only filled containers are plates, the menu, the tooltip and the info pages.
Don't round the corners of boxes, use offset or blurred shadows, or use gradients as shading. The only gradients are the hatched and dotted pattern fills of the distribution levels.
Don't use yellow for decoration or series identity, or colour readout labels when their graph is not on screen.
Don't change weight, size or position to signal an alert.
Don't place anything in the centre of the overlay.
Don't set a label above its value as a heading or eyebrow.
Don't fade an element out in place. It leaves past the nearest edge.
Don't name the camera that inspired the interface anywhere. Describe it only as a camera-like technical readout.
